theme: 3 terms on cleaning up text input: the invisible spaces and newlines around it, the Foundation type that names a group of characters to trim, and comparing text while ignoring capital letters

terms.definition: Characters you can't see, like spaces, tabs and newlines, that often sneak into user input.
terms.example: The login failed because the email had Whitespace at the end.

terms.definition: A Foundation type that describes a group of characters, often used to trim them from the ends of a string.
terms.example: Pass a CharacterSet with the hash sign, so tags come back without it.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let raw = "  #swift!  "
let junk = CharacterSet(charactersIn: "#! ")
print(raw.trimmingCharacters(in: junk))

terms.definition: Comparing two strings while ignoring the difference between capital and small letters.
terms.example: Usernames need a Case Insensitive Comparison, or `Mina` and `mina` both get in.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let a = "Swift", b = "SWIFT"
print(a == b)
let r = a.caseInsensitiveCompare(b)
print(r == .orderedSame)

quizzes.question: In this code, what kind of comparison treats `a` and `b` as the same?
What do you call spaces, tabs and newlines in a string?
Which Foundation type names a group of characters to trim from a string?

video.description:
Learn to explain cleaning up text input in Swift: Whitespace, CharacterSet & Case Insensitive Comparison, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Whitespace - Characters you can't see, like spaces, tabs and newlines, that often sneak into user input.
CharacterSet - A Foundation type that describes a group of characters, often used to trim them from the ends of a string.
Case Insensitive Comparison - Comparing two strings while ignoring the difference between capital and small letters.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: MINA got a name that mina already had. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: The name was taken

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, a user typed `input` and got the name `mina`, which was already taken.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two problems. First, there's Whitespace around it: spaces and a newline.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can't `trimmingCharacters` clean that up for us?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, if you give it a CharacterSet. `whitespacesAndNewlines` covers both.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does it remove the Whitespace in the middle too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, only at the start and the end. The middle stays as it is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So we need a Case Insensitive Comparison.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. `caseInsensitiveCompare` treats them as the same, so the name counts as taken.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Trim the Whitespace with a CharacterSet, then use a Case Insensitive Comparison.
Always trim Whitespace before you check an email.
